tagline: A four-lane run up the old anthracite valley.
intro: Where I-81 splits off at Dunmore, US 6 carries on as a four-lane freeway, the Governor Casey Highway, and bends northeast up the Lackawanna Valley with the towns on one side and the wooded Moosic Mountains on the other. Past Olyphant, Jessup and Archbald it runs through forest, then swings around the east side of Carbondale, with a scenic overlook for westbound traffic.
This is hard-coal country, and the road is the way in to Steamtown National Historic Site, the Pennsylvania Anthracite Heritage Museum and the Lackawanna Coal Mine.

moments.title: Archbald Pothole
moments.text: A miner blasting a shaft in 1884 broke into a 38-foot glacial pothole and fled the rush of water and stones, and nearly 1,000 tons of rounded rocks came out of it.

moments.title: Carbondale
moments.text: The founders of the Delaware and Hudson Canal Company developed the land here, site of the country's first deep-vein anthracite mine, where a mine fire later burned from 1946 into the 1970s.
